text:
1. The passage rewards a reader who pays attention to what is missing from it.
2. Sarah does not appear anywhere in the chapter.
3. The book announces Sarah's death in the verse immediately following the chapter.
4. The scene implies, without stating it, that something in the household did not survive the events on the mountain.
5. Abraham returns to the servants after the events on the mountain.
6. Isaac is not mentioned when Abraham returns to the servants.
7. The text turns away at exactly the moment where a lesser story would linger.
8. Silence in the text is not mere absence but a form of testimony.
9. An opposing reading holds that the chapter simply reflects the conventions of ancient narrative.
10. The opposing reading holds that ancient narrative rarely reports characters' feelings.
11. The opposing reading holds that ancient narrative never explains.
12. The author concedes, with heavy hedging, that the opposing reading may be true in some sense.
13. The narrator elsewhere reports what characters feel.
14. Esau cries out.
15. Jacob is afraid.
16. Joseph weeps.
17. The narrative's reticence in this chapter is deliberate.
18. The text is aware of what it is doing.
19. In this narrative voice, restraint functions as a kind of accusation.
